title: Building and pushing to ECR, immutable tags and image scanning

videos.script: Something broke in production at three in the morning. Which code is running? {{question}} If the answer is a tag called latest, nobody knows. latest is a pointer. The next push moved it, and it says nothing about where it pointed yesterday. {{pointer}} An image is identified by its digest, a hash of its contents. Change one byte and the digest changes. {{digest}} This lesson makes tags behave like names. An immutable repository refuses to move a tag once it is given. And a tag made from the commit hash tells you which code is inside. {{immutable}} Then two habits that keep a registry honest. A scan that fails the pipeline when an image has a serious finding. And a lifecycle policy, so a thousand old builds do not sit on the bill for ever. {{gate}} By the end, you can answer the three a.m. question with one command, and roll back to an image that is byte for byte the one that ran before. {{end}}
